newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Seven has Optus Vision proposals.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Seven has Optus Vision proposals.

text.p: Seven Network Ltd said on Monday it had two offers to enable it to acquire all the shares in pay television operator Optus Vision pending the outcome of future legal action.
Seven said one of the offers is for A$648.74 million and the other is for A$533.80 million. It said it had 10 days to consider and respond to the offers.

Seven is in a legal battle with other Optus Vision shareholders Optus Communications Pty Ltd and U.S. West unit Continental CableVision which both own 46.5 percent and Kerry Packer's Publishing and Broadcasting Ltd, which has a five percent stake in the pay TV group.
The litigation is to be heard in the Supreme Court of New South Wales on February 24, 1997.
Seven has a two percent stake in Optus Vision.
Seven claims the other Optus Vision shareholders breached the Optus Vision shareholders' agreement.

Seven has said if it is successful in the litigation it would be allowed to acquire Optus Communications' stake in Optus Vision at a price which is equal to 85 percent of costs and the average of valuations in the agreement.
Seven is about 23 percent-owned by its chairman Kerry Stokes and 15 percent by News Corp Ltd, which in turn jointly owns the rival Foxtel pay TV network.
